body:
I noticed the following in your log:

> java version "1.8.0_31"

AFAIK, JUnit 5 requires JDK 1.8 update 60 or higher.

Try changing the JDK version for your build and let us know how that goes.

You might find our custom [Travis Config](https://github.com/junit-team/junit5/blob/master/.travis.yml) useful.

It looks like you discovered the solution on your own: https://github.com/bkimminich/kata-botwars/commit/fd3921c5eb07b0be393ecc04a6052c8eb0deb4bb

May we therefore consider this issue resolved?

Thank you! Adding the following to the `.travis.yml` enforced 8u91 but it still didn't execute any tests...

```
addons:
  apt:
    packages:
      - oracle-java8-installer
```

By the way, you need to set the file permissions for `gradlew` appropriately. After doing so locally, I see this with `git diff`:

```
[kata-botwars (master)]$ git diff
diff --git a/gradlew b/gradlew
old mode 100644
new mode 100755
diff --git a/gradlew.bat b/gradlew.bat
old mode 100644
new mode 100755
```

You should execute `./gradlew wrapper`, commit changes, and push to `master`.

I just ran your Gradle build on my Mac with JDK `1.8.0_92`, and I see this:

```
INFO: Discovered TestEngines with IDs [junit5]

Test run finished after 3 ms
[         0 tests found     ]
[         0 tests skipped   ]
[         0 tests started   ]
[         0 tests aborted   ]
[         0 tests successful]
[         0 tests failed    ]
```
I think @bkimminich is referring to the `develop` branch, right?

The problem is has to do with the order in which you execute Gradle commands on the CI server.

I haven't found the exact root problem, but it appears to be an issue with the gradle commands you supply for the coverity scan.

As on the CI server, the following does **not** run the tests locally for me:

```
./gradlew assemble
./gradlew check
```

But the following **does run** the tests locally for me:

```
./gradlew clean assemble check
```

So it looks like the `clean` task is not actually cleaning up everything if you execute `assemble` separately.

In other words, I don't think there is an issue with JUnit 5 but rather with your Gradle task configuration.

That addon for CoverityScan will only be run on the `coverity_scan` branch. From the log I see that `gradle assemble` and `gradle check` were both executed.

To test if the build artifacts are actually there I'll include a CheckStyle violation. If it's a general issue post-`assemble` it shouldn't be found by CheckStyle either.

I don't know why yet, but `project.sourceSets.test.runtimeClasspath.files` only seems to contain one directory, namely `/Users/marcp/Desktop/kata-botwars/botwars-java/build/classes/main`. Thus, test classes are never scanned.

What I can observe is that....

Running `clean assemble` does not compile the test sources.

And then running `clean check` will in fact compile the test sources but seemingly _after_ the `junit5Test` task has been executed. Thus there physically are no tests when the JUnit 5 Gradle plugin executes.

Oddly enough, the following does run the tests... but only for the second execution of `clean check`... which seems a bit like a bug in Gradle or otherwise a bug in the JUnit 5 Gradle plugin.

```
gradlew clean assemble
gradlew clean check
gradlew clean check
```
